thread:
maya: FYI seeing weird service discovery behavior in eu-west after we switched NAT gateway this morning.
arjun: What symptoms?
maya: Some headless services returning node IPs from the wrong AZ, dns SRV/ A lookups inconsistent across clients. Impacting inference replicas.
lee: Any EndpointSlice gaps? can you paste `kubectl get endpointslices -n inference -o wide` from an affected cluster?
maya: Pasting a trimmed output:
```
NAME                     ADDRESSTYPE   PORTS   ENDPOINTS
es-infer-abc123          IPv4          8000    10.0.12.45,10.0.13.32
es-infer-xyz789          IPv4          8000    10.0.22.11
```
maya: But `kubectl get pods -o wide` shows pods for that service in 10.0.13.* and 10.0.22.* only. 10.0.12.45 isn't a current pod.
arjun: That IP looks like an old node that was removed during the NAT migration. endpointslice controller shouldn't have stale endpoints though.
netty: Did the kube-proxy mode flip between `iptables` and `ipvs` during the upgrade? I saw the daemonset rolling earlier.
maya: kube-proxy logs show mixed mode for a short window:
```
I0601 09:12:01 kube-proxy.go:... mode: iptables
I0601 09:12:05 kube-proxy.go:... mode: ipvs
I0601 09:12:07 kube-proxy.go:... mode: iptables
```
lee: If some nodes reported `ipvs` and others `iptables` while endpoints were being reconciled, kube-proxy health probes and endpoint tracking can diverge leading to clients seeing different backends via SRV/A records.
arjun: Also noticed NAT gateway replacement changed egress IPs and we updated route tables + ip-masq config. Could masquerade changes cause kube-proxy to mark endpoints unhealthy? maybe conntrack entries persisted to removed nodes.
maya: Checked conntrack on a problematic node, lots of entries pointing to removed node 10.0.12.45.
infra-bot: (deploy-bot) NAT gateway switch completed 2026-06-01T09:11:50Z. Routes propagated across eu-west-1a/b/c.
netty: Steps: 1) force endpointslice controller resync for namespace inference: `kubectl -n kube-system scale deployment endpointslice-controller --replicas=0 && sleep 10 && scale --replicas=1` 2) purge conntrack on nodes that still have stale flows: `conntrack -D -s 10.0.12.45` 3) roll kube-proxy daemonset with fixed mode (prefer ipvs) so modes don't mix during rolling upgrades.
lee: Agree. Also recommend temporarily cordoning drained nodes that still advertise old IPs and run `kubectl delete endpointslice <name>` if they don't reconcile after controller restart.
maya: Doing the resync + small kube-proxy roll now. I'll report back in ~5m.
maya: Resync done, conntrack purge on 3 nodes, kube-proxy rolled with `--proxy-mode=ipvs`.
arjun: Any improvement?
maya: Clients now get consistent SRV answers, endpoint IPs match current pods. Latency spike settled.
netty: Follow-up: we should add a preflight during NAT/egress changes to verify EndpointSlice reconciliation and ensure kube-proxy mode is pinned during daemonset rolling.
lee: Filed INFRA-982: "Verify endpointslice/kube-proxy stability during NAT gateway maintenance" and added checklist.
maya: Thanks team :thumbsup:
infra-bot: Incident note appended to the maintenance ticket.
